questions.question: Meristematic tissues are found only in a specific region. On the basis of position, which is NOT a meristematic tissue type?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Basal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meristematic tissues** are a group of cells that have the ability to divide continuously throughout their life. Based on their **position** in the plant body, they are primarily classified into three types: **Apical**, **Intercalary**, and **Lateral** meristems.
 
• **Apical Meristem**: These are situated at the **growing tips of stems and roots** (shoot apex and root apex). They are responsible for the **increase in length** of the plant, known as **primary growth**. ***Hence, Apical is a correct type of meristematic tissue.***
 
• **Intercalary Meristem**: These are located at the **base of leaves** or **internodes** (e.g., in grasses). They help in the **regeneration of parts** removed by grazing herbivores and contribute to the elongation of organs. ***Hence, Intercalary is a correct type of meristematic tissue.***
 
• **Lateral Meristem**: These occur on the **lateral sides** of stems and roots. They are responsible for **increasing the girth** or thickness of the plant, which is known as **secondary growth**. Examples include **vascular cambium** and **cork cambium**. ***Hence, Lateral is a correct type of meristematic tissue.***
 
• **Basal**: In the standard botanical classification of meristems based on position, **Basal** is not recognized as a primary distinct category. While some specific tissues in certain plants might be located at the base, the three fundamental types remain Apical, Intercalary, and Lateral. ***Hence, Basal is NOT a standard meristematic tissue type based on position.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Meristematic Cells**:
 
 
• The cells are very active, possessing **dense cytoplasm**, **thin cellulose walls**, and **prominent nuclei**.
 
• They generally **lack vacuoles** because they do not need to store food or provide structural support, as their primary function is **cell division**.
 
• The term **Meristem** was coined by **Karl Wilhelm von Nägeli** in the year **1858**.
 
 
 
• **Permanent Tissues**:
 
 
• Once meristematic cells take up a specific role and lose the ability to divide, they form **permanent tissues**. This process is called **differentiation**.
 
• **Simple Permanent Tissues** consist of cells similar in structure (e.g., **Parenchyma**, **Collenchyma**, and **Sclerenchyma**).
 
• **Complex Permanent Tissues** consist of more than one type of cell working together (e.g., **Xylem** and **Phloem**).
 
 
 
• **Primary vs. Secondary Growth**:
 
 
• **Primary growth** occurs due to the activity of **Apical** and **Intercalary** meristems, leading to the elongation of the plant body.
 
• **Secondary growth** is typical in **dicotyledons** and **gymnosperms**, facilitated by **Lateral meristems** like the **Cambium**, which increases the diameter of the plant.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Location Summary**:
 
 
• **Apical Meristem**: Found at **root and shoot tips**.
 
• **Intercalary Meristem**: Found at the **nodes** or **leaf bases** of **monocots**.
 
• **Lateral Meristem**: Found in the **vascular bundles** and **cork layer** of **woody plants**.
 
 
 
• **Functions**:
 
 
• The **Vascular Cambium** produces **secondary xylem** (wood) and **secondary phloem**.
 
• The **Cork Cambium** (Phellogen) produces the **periderm**, which replaces the **epidermis** in older stems and roots.

questions.question: Which of the following hydrocarbons are organic compounds with elements __________?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**both hydrogen and carbon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Hydrocarbons** are organic compounds that are composed exclusively of the elements **carbon** and **hydrogen**. They are considered the fundamental compounds of **organic chemistry**.

• The **carbon** atoms in a hydrocarbon provide the structural framework or **covalent backbone**, while the **hydrogen** atoms are attached to the carbon atoms to satisfy their **tetravalency**.

• Because carbon has a **valency of 4**, it can form four stable **covalent bonds**, allowing for the formation of long chains, branched structures, or rings. **Hydrogen**, with a **valency of 1**, fills the remaining bonding sites.

• Hydrocarbons do not contain other elements like **oxygen**, **nitrogen**, or **sulfur** in their pure form; if these elements are present, the compounds are classified as **hydrocarbon derivatives** or other functional groups (e.g., alcohols, carboxylic acids).

• They serve as the primary source of **energy** for the modern world, being the main components of **petroleum** and **natural gas**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Classification of Hydrocarbons:**

• **Saturated Hydrocarbons (Alkanes):** These contain only **single bonds** between carbon atoms. Their general formula is **CnH2n+2**. Examples include **Methane (CH4)** and **Ethane (C2H6)**.

• **Unsaturated Hydrocarbons:** These contain **double bonds** (**Alkenes**, formula **CnH2n**) or **triple bonds** (**Alkynes**, formula **CnH2n-2**). An example of an alkene is **Ethene (C2H4)**, and an alkyne is **Ethyne (C2H2)**.

• **Aromatic Hydrocarbons:** These are cyclic hydrocarbons with **delocalized pi electrons**, such as **Benzene (C6H6)**. They are known for their stable ring structures and distinct odors.

• **Physical State and Properties:**

• The physical state of a hydrocarbon depends on its **molecular weight**. Low-molecular-weight hydrocarbons (C1 to C4) like **Methane** and **Butane** are **gases** at **room temperature**.

• Intermediate-weight hydrocarbons (C5 to C17) are generally **liquids** (like **Gasoline** or **Hexane**), while those with 18 or more carbon atoms are **solids** (like **Paraffin wax**).

• Hydrocarbons are generally **non-polar** and **hydrophobic**, meaning they do not dissolve in **water** but are soluble in organic solvents.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Combustion:** When hydrocarbons undergo **complete combustion** in the presence of **oxygen**, they produce **carbon dioxide (CO2)**, **water (H2O)**, and a significant amount of **heat energy**. This property makes them excellent **fuels**.

• **Sources:** The primary natural sources of hydrocarbons are **fossil fuels**, which were formed over **millions of years** from the remains of ancient marine organisms and plants under high **pressure** and **temperature**.

• **Isomerism:** Hydrocarbons can exhibit **structural isomerism**, where compounds have the same **molecular formula** but different **structural arrangements**, leading to different physical and chemical properties.

• **Industrial Uses:** Beyond fuel, they are used as **feedstock** in the **petrochemical industry** to manufacture **plastics**, **synthetic fibers**, **rubbers**, **solvents**, and **lubricants**.
</ul

questions.question: What is the transfer of pollen grain from one flower to another flower called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cross pollination**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cross pollination**, scientifically referred to as **Allogamy**, is the process where **pollen grains** are transferred from the **anther** of a flower on one plant to the **stigma** of a flower on a **different plant** of the **same species**.
 
• Unlike self-pollination, this method relies heavily on external **pollinating agents** such as **insects**, **wind**, **water**, or **animals** to bridge the distance between two separate plants.
 
• The primary advantage of **cross pollination** is that it facilitates **genetic recombination**, leading to **genetic diversity** in the offspring, which helps the species adapt better to changing environmental conditions.
 
• Plants that practice cross-pollination often have specific **features** to attract pollinators, such as **brightly colored petals**, **scent**, and **nectar**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Cross pollination.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Self-pollination:**
 
 
• This occurs when **pollen grains** from the **anther** are transferred to the **stigma** of the **same flower** or another flower on the **same plant**.
 
• It does not require external agents and is common in plants where male and female parts mature at the same time.
 
 
 
• **Autogamy:**
 
 
• **Autogamy** is a specific type of **self-pollination** where the transfer happens within a **single flower**.
 
• It ensures seed set even in the absence of pollinators but results in **inbreeding depression** over several generations due to lack of variation.
 
 
 
• **Agents of Pollination:**
 
 
• **Biotic Agents**: These include living organisms like **bees**, **butterflies**, **birds**, and **bats**. Pollination by insects is called **Entomophily**, while pollination by birds is **Ornithophily**.
 
• **Abiotic Agents**: These are non-living factors like **wind** (**Anemophily**) and **water** (**Hydrophily**). **Maize** and **wheat** are classic **examples** of wind-pollinated crops.
 
 
 
• **Geitonogamy:**
 
 
• This is the transfer of **pollen grains** from the **anther** to the **stigma** of another flower on the **same plant**. While functionally it is cross-pollination (requiring a pollinator), genetically it is similar to **autogamy**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cleistogamous Flowers**: These are **flowers** that never open (e.g., **Viola**, **Oxalis**, and **Commelina**). In such flowers, the **anther** and **stigma** lie close to each other, ensuring **autogamy** occurs without the need for any external agent.
 
• **Chasmogamous Flowers**: These are **open flowers** with exposed **anthers** and **stigma**, making them available for both **self-pollination** and **cross-pollination**.
 
• **Hybrid Vigor**: Also known as **heterosis**, this is the increased **function** or **vitality** of a hybrid offspring compared to its parents, often achieved through **cross pollination**.
 
• **Self-Incompatibility**: This is a **genetic mechanism** that prevents **self-pollen** from fertilizing the **ovules** of the same flower by inhibiting pollen germination, thereby promoting **cross pollination**.
</ul

questions.question: The distance between the optical centre of a lens and its principal focus is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**focal length**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The distance between the **optical centre** of a lens and its **principal focus** is termed the **focal length**.
 
• It is commonly represented by the lowercase letter **'f'**.
 
• The **SI unit** for measuring focal length is the **metre (m)**, though it is often expressed in **centimetres (cm)** in laboratory settings.
 
• In a **convex lens** (converging lens), the focal length is taken as **positive** because the light rays actually converge at the focus on the opposite side of the lens.
 
• In a **concave lens** (diverging lens), the focal length is taken as **negative** because the light rays appear to diverge from a focus located on the same side as the object.
 
• The **principal focus** is the specific point on the **principal axis** where rays of light parallel to the axis meet or appear to meet after passing through the lens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aperture:**
 
 
• The **aperture** refers to the effective **diameter** of the circular outline of a spherical lens.
 
• It determines the **amount of light** that passes through the lens; a larger aperture allows more light to enter, resulting in a brighter image.
 
 
 
• **Magnification:**
 
 
• **Magnification (m)** is defined as the ratio of the **height of the image** to the **height of the object**.
 
• It can also be expressed as the ratio of **image distance (v)** to **object distance (u)**.
 
• A **negative** magnification indicates a **real and inverted** image, while a **positive** magnification indicates a **virtual and erect** image.
 
 
 
• **Radius of Curvature:**
 
 
• The **radius of curvature (R)** is the radius of the **imaginary sphere** of which the lens surface forms a part.
 
• A lens has two surfaces, and therefore has two radii of curvature, often denoted as **R1** and **R2**.
 
 
 
• **Optical Centre:**
 
 
• The **optical centre** is the **geometric centre** of a lens.
 
• Any ray of light passing through the **optical centre** of a lens does not suffer any **deviation** and emerges along its original path.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lens Formula:** The mathematical relationship between the **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by the formula **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**.
 
• **Power of a Lens:** The **power (P)** of a lens is the reciprocal of its focal length in metres (**P = 1/f**). The unit of power is the **Dioptre (D)**.
 
• **Sign Convention:** According to the **Cartesian sign convention**, distances measured in the direction of incident light are **positive**, while those measured against the direction of incident light are **negative**.
 
• **Relationship with R:** For a **thin lens** with both sides having equal curvature, the **radius of curvature (R)** is approximately **twice** the focal length (**R = 2f**).
</ul

questions.question: Which organism is a key indicator of a healthy aquatic ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fish**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fish** are widely recognized as primary **bioindicators** for assessing the health of **aquatic ecosystems** because they are highly sensitive to variations in their environment.
 
• They occupy various **trophic levels**, acting as **primary consumers**, **secondary consumers**, and **top predators**. Because they are at the top of many **aquatic food chains**, their health reflects the overall status of the **biological community**.
 
• Changes in **water quality** parameters, such as **dissolved oxygen (DO)**, **pH levels**, **water temperature**, and the presence of **dissolved solids**, directly affect **fish physiology** and **reproduction**.
 
• Monitoring **fish species diversity** and **population density** provides a long-term record of **environmental stress**. Unlike chemical tests that provide a "snapshot" of water quality, **fish** provide a continuous **biomonitoring** history of a **habitat**.
 
• The presence or absence of specific **indicator species** can signify specific conditions; for instance, the presence of **Salmon** or **Trout** usually indicates **cold, well-oxygenated, and clean water**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lichen**:
 
 
• These are **symbiotic organisms** composed of **fungi** and **algae** or **cyanobacteria**.
 
• They are key indicators of **air quality**. Because they lack a **waxy cuticle**, they absorb **pollutants** directly from the **atmosphere**.
 
• They are particularly sensitive to **sulfur dioxide (SO2)**; hence, their absence in **urban areas** often indicates high **atmospheric pollution**.
 
 
 
• **Earthworm**:
 
 
• These organisms are vital indicators of **soil health** and **terrestrial ecosystem** stability.
 
• Their presence indicates high levels of **organic matter** and good **soil aeration**.
 
• They are sensitive to **pesticides** and **heavy metal contamination** in the **lithosphere**, making them essential for assessing **agricultural sustainability**.
 
 
 
• **Cockroach**:
 
 
• While they are biological organisms, they are generally considered **pests** rather than positive **ecological indicators**.
 
• They are known for their **extreme resilience** and ability to survive in **unhygienic conditions**, often serving as indicators of **poor sanitation** in **urban environments**.
 
 
 
• **Benthic Macroinvertebrates**:
 
 
• Organisms like **mayflies**, **stoneflies**, and **caddisflies** are also used alongside **fish** to determine **water quality**.
 
• The **Biotic Index** is often calculated based on the **sensitivity** of these organisms to **organic pollution** and **sedimentation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Biomagnification**: This is a process where the concentration of **toxic substances** (like **mercury** or **DDT**) increases as it moves up the **food chain**. **Fish** are often monitored to detect these **heavy metals** before they reach **human consumers**.
 
• **Eutrophication**: A healthy **fish population** helps prevent the overgrowth of **algae**. However, excessive **nutrients** (nitrogen and phosphorus) lead to **algal blooms**, which deplete **oxygen** and cause mass **fish kills**, signaling a **disturbed ecosystem**.
 
• **Global Context**: The **Index of Biological Integrity (IBI)** is a scientific tool that uses **fish communities** to grade the **ecological health** of **running waters** (rivers and streams) worldwide, including in **India** and the **USA**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following processes results in the formation of two identical daughter cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitosis** is a type of **cell division** in which a single **parent cell** divides to produce **two genetically identical daughter cells**. These cells contain the same number of **chromosomes** and the same **genetic information** as the parent cell. ***Hence, the correct answer is Mitosis.***
 
• This process is also known as **equational division** because the **chromosomal number** is maintained throughout the division (e.g., a **diploid cell** produces two **diploid daughter cells**).
 
• Mitosis occurs primarily in **somatic cells** (vegetative cells) and is essential for the **growth**, **development**, and **tissue repair** of multicellular organisms.
 
• The process consists of four main stages: **Prophase**, **Metaphase**, **Anaphase**, and **Telophase**, followed by the physical splitting of the cell.
 
• It ensures that every new cell generated in the body has an **exact copy** of the **DNA**, maintaining **genomic stability** across generations of cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Meiosis:**
 
 
• **Meiosis** is a **reductional division** that occurs in **germ cells** (reproductive cells) to produce **gametes** (sperm and egg).
 
• Unlike mitosis, it results in **four non-identical daughter cells**, each having **half the number of chromosomes** (**haploid**) of the original parent cell.
 
• It introduces **genetic variation** through a process called **crossing over** or **recombination** during **Prophase I**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Cytokinesis and Karyokinesis:**
 
 
• **Karyokinesis** is the division of the **nucleus**, whereas **cytokinesis** is the division of the **cytoplasm**.
 
• If **cytokinesis** occurs without **karyokinesis**, the cell would simply split without the **replicated DNA** being partitioned, leading to daughter cells that lack a full set of instructions or a nucleus. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Fertilisation:**
 
 
• **Fertilisation** is the process of **fusion** of a male gamete with a female gamete to form a **zygote**.
 
• This is not a division process but a **fusion process** that restores the **diploid** number of chromosomes and creates a **genetically unique** individual. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Cell Cycle:** Mitosis is a part of the **M-phase** of the **cell cycle**. Before entering mitosis, a cell undergoes **Interphase**, which includes the **G1 phase**, **S phase** (where **DNA replication** occurs), and **G2 phase**.
 
• **Stages of Mitosis:**
 
 
• **Prophase:** Chromatin condenses into visible **chromosomes**, and the **nuclear envelope** begins to break down.
 
• **Metaphase:** Chromosomes align at the **equatorial plate** (metaphase plate) of the cell.
 
• **Anaphase:** **Sister chromatids** are pulled apart toward opposite **poles** of the cell.
 
• **Telophase:** Two new **nuclear membranes** form around the separated chromatids, which begin to de-condense back into chromatin.
 
 
 
• **Significance:** In **unicellular organisms** like **Amoeba**, mitosis is a method of **asexual reproduction**, producing offspring that are **clones** of the parent.
</ul

questions.question: What advantage does asexual reproduction provide in a stable environment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rapid and identical reproduction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asexual reproduction** is a biological process by which an organism creates a **genetically identical** copy of itself without the contribution of genetic material from another individual.
 
• In a **stable environment**, where conditions such as food supply, temperature, and habitat remain constant, the most significant advantage is the ability for **rapid population growth**. Because organisms do not need to spend time or energy finding a **mate**, they can reproduce much faster than sexually reproducing species.
 
• The production of **identical offspring** (clones) ensures that if the parent possesses a **genotype** that is well-adapted to the current environment, all offspring will inherit those same successful traits. This maintains **genetic stability** across generations. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Adaptation to new environments** and **genetic variation** are primary advantages of **sexual reproduction**, not asexual. Variation allows a species to survive if environmental conditions change. ***Hence, statement 1 and 4 are incorrect.***
 
• **Sexual diversity** is the result of **meiosis** and the fusion of gametes, which does not occur in asexual reproduction. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Modes of Asexual Reproduction**:

__
 
• A **balanced chemical equation** is one where the number of atoms of each element on the **reactant side** (left) is equal to the number of atoms of the same element on the **product side** (right).
 
• In the equation **3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂**, let us count the atoms:
 
 
• **Iron (Fe)**: There are **3 atoms** on the reactant side and **3 atoms** in **Fe₃O₄** on the product side.
 
• **Oxygen (O)**: There are **4 atoms** in **4H₂O** on the reactant side and **4 atoms** in **Fe₃O₄** on the product side.
 
• **Hydrogen (H)**: There are **8 atoms** (4 × 2) in **4H₂O** on the reactant side and **8 atoms** (4 × 2) in **4H₂** on the product side.
 
 ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***
 
 
• In **Option 1 (Fe + H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + H₂)**, the number of **Fe** atoms (1 vs 3) and **O** atoms (1 vs 4) are not equal. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• In **Option 2 (2Fe + 3H₂O → 2Fe₃O₄ + 3H₂)**, the **Fe** atoms (2 vs 6) and **O** atoms (3 vs 8) are unbalanced. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

questions.question: Truck and motorbus tyres are designed to be much wider than car tyres, while cutting tools and nails are designed with sharp, small tips. This contrast in design illustrates the principle that __________.

options.text: thrust is directly proportional to the area of contact
larger thrust always results in lower pressure
the same thrust acting on a smaller area exerts a larger pressure
pressure is inversely proportional to the mass of the object

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the same thrust acting on a smaller area exerts a larger pressure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pressure** is defined as the **thrust** (perpendicular force) acting per unit **area** of a surface. The relationship between these variables is represented by the formula: **Pressure = Thrust / Area**.
 
• For a given amount of **force** or **thrust**, the **pressure** produced is **inversely proportional** to the **area** of the surface on which it acts. This means as the **area** decreases, the **pressure** increases, and as the **area** increases, the **pressure** decreases.
 
• **Nails and Cutting Tools**: These are designed with **sharp, small tips** to minimize the **contact area**. When a **force** is applied, the **small area** results in a very **high pressure**, allowing the tool to easily penetrate or cut through objects like wood or metal. ***Hence, the statement that the same thrust acting on a smaller area exerts a larger pressure is correct.***
 
• **Truck and Motorbus Tyres**: Large vehicles carry a significant amount of **weight** (thrust). They are equipped with **much wider tyres** to increase the **surface area** in contact with the road. By increasing the **area**, the **pressure** exerted on the ground is reduced, preventing the tyres from sinking into soft surfaces and reducing wear and tear.
 
• Regarding the other options: **Thrust** is a **force** and is not directly proportional to **area** in a physical definition sense (Option 1 is incorrect). Larger **thrust** usually results in **higher pressure** if the area is constant (Option 2 is incorrect). **Pressure** is related to **mass** through weight, but the direct proportionality is with **force** and **area** (Option 4 is incorrect).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Definition of Thrust**: **Thrust** is the **force** acting **perpendicularly** to a surface. While **force** can act in any direction, **thrust** specifically refers to the normal component. The **SI unit** of **thrust** is the **Newton (N)**.
 
• **Units of Pressure**: The **SI unit** of **pressure** is the **Pascal (Pa)**, which is defined as **one Newton per square metre (1 N/m²)**. It is named after the **17th-century** physicist and mathematician **Blaise Pascal**.
 
• **Real-world Applications**: 
 
 
• **School Bags**: They are provided with **broad straps** so that the **weight** of the bag falls over a larger **area** of the shoulder, resulting in **less pressure** and less pain for the student.
 
• **Foundations of Buildings**: High-rise structures have **wide foundations** to distribute the immense **thrust** of the building over a large **area** of soil, ensuring the **pressure** does not exceed the bearing capacity of the ground.
 
• **Sleeper Tracks**: Railway tracks are laid on **wooden or concrete sleepers** to spread the **force** of the train over a larger **area**, reducing the **pressure** on the ground below.
 
 
 
• **Pressure in Fluids**: Unlike solids that exert **pressure** only downwards due to **gravity**, **fluids** (liquids and gases) exert **pressure** in all directions on the walls of their container. This is the basis for **hydraulic systems** used in **car brakes** and **heavy machinery**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Inversely Proportional**: It is crucial to remember that **Pressure** and **Area** have an **inverse relationship**. If you double the **area** while keeping the **thrust** constant, the **pressure** is halved.
 
• **Force vs. Pressure**: People often confuse these two terms. **Force** is the total impact, while **pressure** is how "concentrated" that impact is over a specific **surface**. 
 
• **Atmospheric Pressure**: Even air exerts **pressure**. At **sea level**, the **atmospheric pressure** is approximately **101,325 Pa**. This **pressure** decreases as **altitude** increases because the **mass** of the air column above decreases.

• **Discovery:** The **Endoplasmic Reticulum** was first observed by **Keith R. Porter**, **Albert Claude**, and **Ernest F. Fullam** in **1945** using electron microscopy.
 
• **Metabolic Variation:** The ratio of **SER** to **RER** in a cell depends on the cell's **metabolic activity**. For example, **sebaceous glands** (which produce skin oils) are rich in **Smooth ER**, while **pancreatic cells** (which produce digestive enzymes) are rich in **Rough ER**.
 
• **Signaling:** The **calcium storage** function of the **SER** is crucial for **intracellular signaling**, affecting processes like **cell death (apoptosis)** and **gene expression**.

The correct answer is __**Electrolysis of molten aluminium oxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The extraction of **Aluminium** from its primary ore, **Bauxite**, is primarily carried out using the **Hall-Heroult process**.
 
• This process involves the **Electrolysis** of **Alumina (Aluminium Oxide)** which is dissolved in a molten bath of **Cryolite** and **Fluorspar**.
 
• Aluminium is a highly **reactive metal** (high in the **reactivity series**), meaning it forms very stable bonds with oxygen that cannot be broken by **carbon reduction**; therefore, **electrolytic reduction** is necessary.
 
• In the electrolytic cell, the **Cathode** is a carbon lining at the bottom where **molten aluminium** is deposited and collected.
 
• The **Anode** consists of **Graphite rods** dipped into the electrolyte, where **oxygen gas** is liberated and subsequently reacts with the carbon rods to form **Carbon Dioxide**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***

__
 
• **Bauxite Refining (Bayer Process):**
 
 
• Before electrolysis, **Bauxite** must be purified into **Alumina** using the **Bayer Process**, which involves heating the ore with **Sodium Hydroxide**.
 
• This process removes impurities like **Iron Oxide** (red mud) and **Silica** to ensure the final metal is of high purity.
 
 
 
• **The Role of Cryolite:**
 
 
• Pure **Alumina** has a very high **melting point** of about **2050 degrees Celsius**, making electrolysis difficult and expensive.
 
• Adding **molten Cryolite (Sodium Aluminium Fluoride)** acts as a **solvent** and lowers the **melting point** to approximately **950 degrees Celsius**, significantly reducing **energy consumption** and increasing **electrical conductivity**.
 
 
 
• **Metal Reactivity and Extraction:**
 
 
• Metals like **Gold** and **Silver** occur in a **native state** or can be extracted by heating.
 
• Metals in the middle of the series like **Iron** and **Zinc** are extracted using **Carbon reduction** (smelting).
 
• Metals at the top of the series, including **Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, and Aluminium**, must be extracted via **electrolysis** of their molten salts or oxides.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Aluminium Characteristics:** It is the **most abundant metal** in the **Earth's crust** and the **third most abundant element** overall. It is valued for its **low density**, **high thermal conductivity**, and **corrosion resistance** due to a protective **oxide layer**.
 
• **Industrial Use:** Due to its lightweight nature, it is used extensively in **aerospace**, **automotive industries**, **packaging (foil and cans)**, and **electrical transmission lines**.
 
• **Anode Consumption:** A significant part of the cost in this process is the **regular replacement of graphite anodes**, as they are consumed by the oxygen produced during the reaction, forming **CO2 gas**.
 
• **Recycling:** Extracting aluminium is extremely **energy-intensive**. However, **recycling aluminium** requires only about **5 percent** of the energy needed to produce it from raw bauxite, making it one of the most sustainable metals to reuse.

questions.question: The SI unit of Power is watt (W). As per the relation of work-power, one watt is equivalent to _____________.

__
 
• **Power** is defined as the **rate of doing work** or the **rate at which energy is transferred or transformed**. It measures how fast work is being done by an object or a machine.
 
• The mathematical formula for power is **P = W / t**, where **P** stands for **Power**, **W** stands for **Work done**, and **t** represents the **time taken** to complete that work.
 
• Since the **SI unit** of **Work** is the **Joule (J)** and the **SI unit** of **Time** is the **second (s)**, the unit of power is **Joule/second**.
 
• The **SI unit** of **Power** is the **Watt (W)**, named after the **Scottish scientist James Watt**. By definition, **1 Watt** is equal to the power of an agent that performs work at the rate of **1 Joule per second (1 J/s)**. *Hence, option 3 is correct.*
 
• If an agent consumes **one Joule** of energy in **one second**, its power is said to be **1 Watt**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Kilowatt-hour (kWh)**: This is often confused with power, but it is actually a unit of **Energy**. It represents the amount of energy consumed by a **1000-watt** appliance in **one hour**. **1 kWh** is equal to **3.6 x 1,000,000 Joules**.
 
• **Horsepower (hp)**: This is a non-SI unit of power used primarily in the automotive and engineering industries. **1 Horsepower (British)** is approximately equal to **746 Watts**.
 
• **Dimensional Formula**: The dimensional formula for power is **[ML²T⁻³]**, derived from the dimensions of work **[ML²T⁻²]** divided by time **[T]**.
 
• **Scalar Quantity**: Power is a **scalar quantity** because it only has **magnitude** and does not require a direction to be fully described.
 
• **Larger Units**: For industrial purposes, power is often expressed in **kilowatts (kW)**, where **1 kW = 1,000 W**, or **megawatts (MW)**, where **1 MW = 1,000,000 W**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best explains why all atoms of an element are represented by the same symbol?

options.text: Because they have the same number of protons in their nucleus
Because they have the same number of neutrons in the nucleus
Because their mass numbers are always the same
Because they have identical physical properties

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Because they have the same number of protons in their nucleus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The identity of an **element** is fundamentally defined by its **atomic number**, which is the total number of **protons** found in the nucleus of its atoms.
 
• All atoms of a specific element must have the same number of **protons**. For instance, every **Carbon** atom has exactly **6 protons**; if it had a different number, it would be a different element. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Atoms of the same element can possess different numbers of **neutrons** in their nuclei; these variations are called **isotopes**. Therefore, the number of **neutrons** is not a defining characteristic for the element's symbol. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **mass number** is the sum of **protons** and **neutrons**. Because **isotopes** have different numbers of **neutrons**, atoms of the same element can have different **mass numbers** (e.g., **Carbon-12** and **Carbon-14**). ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• While atoms of the same element share the same **chemical properties** due to their **electron configuration**, they do not have identical **physical properties**. **Isotopes** of an element differ in **mass**, **density**, and sometimes **radioactivity**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The **chemical symbol** (such as **H**, **He**, **Li**) serves as a shorthand notation for an element and applies to all its **isotopes** because they all share the same **atomic number**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atomic Number (Z):**
 
 
• The concept of the **atomic number** being the identifying trait of an element was solidified by the work of **Henry Moseley** in **1913**.
 
• In the **Modern Periodic Table**, elements are arranged in increasing order of their **atomic number (Z)** rather than **atomic mass**.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes and Isobars:**
 
 
• **Isotopes**: Atoms with the same **atomic number** but different **mass numbers** (e.g., **Protium**, **Deuterium**, and **Tritium** for **Hydrogen**).
 
• **Isobars**: Atoms of different elements (different **atomic numbers**) that happen to have the same **mass number** (e.g., **Calcium-40** and **Argon-40**).
 
 
 
• **Subatomic Particles:**
 
 
• **Protons**: Positively charged particles discovered by **Ernest Rutherford** (often credited alongside **Goldstein**). Their number defines the **element**.
 
• **Neutrons**: Neutral particles discovered by **James Chadwick** in **1932**. They contribute to the **nuclear stability** and **mass**.
 
• **Electrons**: Negatively charged particles discovered by **J.J. Thomson**. In a **neutral atom**, the number of **electrons** equals the number of **protons**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Chemical Reactivity**: The **chemical behavior** of an atom is determined by the **valence electrons**, which are dictated by the **atomic number** in a neutral state. This is why **isotopes** react almost identically in chemical processes.
 
• **Nuclide Notation**: When representing a specific atom, the **mass number (A)** is written as a **superscript** and the **atomic number (Z)** as a **subscript** to the left of the **element symbol** (X).
 
• **Nuclear Charge**: The **protons** provide the entire positive charge of the nucleus, which exerts the **electrostatic pull** on the **electrons**, determining the size and structure of the atom.

questions.question: Estimate the concentration of the solution in terms of mass by mass percentage if 50 g of common salt is dissolved in 300 g of water.

• Total **mass of the solution** = Mass of solute + Mass of solvent = **50 g** + **300 g** = **350 g**.
 
• The formula for **mass by mass percentage** is: (Mass of solute / Mass of solution) × **100**.
 
• Applying the values: (**50** / **350**) × **100** = (**1** / **7**) × **100**.
 
• Calculation results in approximately **14.2857%**, which is rounded to **14.28%**. ***Hence, the correct option is 14.28%.***

__

• **Solute**: The substance that is dissolved in a solvent to form a solution. In this example, **common salt (Sodium Chloride)** is the solute, weighing **50 g**.
 
• **Solvent**: The medium in which the solute is dissolved. **Water** is often called the **universal solvent** due to its ability to dissolve a wide variety of substances. Here, its mass is **300 g**.
 
 
 
• **Methods of Expressing Concentration**:
 
 
• **Mass by Volume Percentage**: This is the mass of solute dissolved in **100 mL** of the solution. It is commonly used in medicine and pharmacy.
 
• **Volume by Volume Percentage**: Used when both the solute and solvent are liquids (e.g., **alcohol** in water).
 
• **Molarity**: A more advanced unit representing the number of **moles of solute** per **liter** of solution.
 
 
 
• **Types of Solutions based on Concentration**:
 
 
• **Dilute Solution**: Contains a small amount of solute relative to the solvent.
 
• **Concentrated Solution**: Contains a large amount of dissolved solute.
 
• **Saturated Solution**: A solution in which no more solute can be dissolved at a **specific temperature**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Solubility**: The maximum amount of solute that can be dissolved in **100 g** of solvent at a given **temperature**. For most solids like **salt**, solubility increases with an **increase in temperature**.
 
• **Common Salt (NaCl)**: It is an **ionic compound**. When dissolved in water, it undergoes **dissociation** into **sodium ions (Na+)** and **chloride ions (Cl-)**, allowing the solution to **conduct electricity**.
 
• **Homogeneous Nature**: A true solution, like salt in water, is **homogeneous**, meaning the particles are distributed uniformly at the molecular level and cannot be seen with the **naked eye**.
 
• **Physical Change**: Dissolving salt in water is generally considered a **physical change** because the salt can be recovered through the process of **evaporation** or **distillation**.
 
• **Mass Conservation**: In any solution process, the **Law of Conservation of Mass** applies; the total mass of the final solution is exactly equal to the sum of the masses of the components added.

questions.question: The number 8,33,525 is NOT divisible by:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To check divisibility by 15, the number must be divisible by both 3 and 5.

Sum of digits of 833525 = 8 + 3 + 3 + 5 + 2 + 5 = 26.

Since 26 is not divisible by 3, the number 833525 is not divisible by 3.

Thus, it cannot be divisible by 15.

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The number is 833525.

**Concept Used:**

If a number is divisible by two co-prime factors of a composite number, it is also divisible by that composite number.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let's check divisibility by 25:

⇒ The last two digits are 25. Since 25 is perfectly divisible by 25, the number 833525 is divisible by 25.

⇒ Let's check divisibility by 55 (which is 5 × 11):

⇒ The last digit is 5, so it is divisible by 5.

⇒ Sum of odd place digits = 8 + 3 + 2 = 13.

⇒ Sum of even place digits = 3 + 5 + 5 = 13.

⇒ Difference = 13 − 13 = 0. Since the difference is 0, it is divisible by 11. Thus, the number is divisible by 55.

⇒ Let's check divisibility by 35 (which is 5 × 7):

⇒ The last digit is 5, so it is divisible by 5.

⇒ 833525 ÷ 7 = 119075. Since the remainder is 0, it is perfectly divisible by 7. Thus, the number is divisible by 35.

⇒ Let's check divisibility by 15 (which is 3 × 5):

⇒ Sum of digits = 8 + 3 + 3 + 5 + 2 + 5 = 26.

⇒ Since 26 is not divisible by 3, 833525 is NOT divisible by 15.

**∴ The correct answer is 15.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule for 3 and 9

A number is divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3 or 9, respectively.

Divisibility Rule for 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of its digits at odd places and the sum of its digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

Divisibility Rule for 7

Form groups of 3 digits from right to left, and find the alternating sum and difference. If the result is divisible by 7, then the original number is also divisible by 7.

Composite Number Divisibility

If a number is divisible by two co-prime numbers (a and b), it is always divisible by their product (a × b).

• The day marks the successful conclusion of **Operation Vijay**, during which **India** regained control of the high outposts in the **Kargil-Dras** sector that had been illegally occupied by **Pakistani** intruders.
 
• The **Kargil War** lasted for more than **60 days**, starting in **May 1999** and officially ending on **July 26, 1999**, when **Pakistan** was completely evicted from **Indian** territory.
 
• On **26 July 2025**, **India** observed the **26th anniversary** of this historic victory, paying tribute to the **527 soldiers** who made the supreme sacrifice for the nation.
 
• The main celebrations are typically held at the **Kargil War Memorial** located in **Dras**, **Ladakh**, which is often referred to as the second coldest inhabited place in the world. ***Hence, the correct answer is Kargil Vijay Diwas.***

• **Operation Safed Sagar**: This was the code name assigned to the **Indian Air Force's** role in acting jointly with the **Indian Army** during the conflict.

• **Political Leadership:** During the **1999** war, **Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee** was the **Prime Minister of India**, and **George Fernandes** served as the **Defence Minister**.
 
• **Geographic Location:** The conflict took place in the **Kargil district** of **Ladakh**, along the **Line of Control (LoC)**. Strategic peaks like **Tiger Hill** and **Tololing** were key battlegrounds.
 
• **Global Significance:** The **Kargil War** was the first direct conventional war between two **nuclear-armed** nations, drawing significant international attention and diplomatic pressure on **Pakistan** to withdraw.

• The opening of the park generally occurs in a phased manner, starting with **Jeep Safaris** in the **Bagori** and **Kohora** ranges, while **Elephant Safaris** are introduced later once the ground is sufficiently firm.
 
• This announcement is crucial for the tourism industry in **Assam**, as the park remains closed from **May** to **September** every year due to the overflow of the **Brahmaputra River**.
 
• The **Bagori Range** is highly popular among tourists specifically for sightings of the **Great Indian One-Horned Rhinoceros**, as the visibility in this grassland-dominated range is exceptionally high.

• **Kaziranga National Park**: Located in the **Golaghat** and **Nagaon** districts of the state of **Assam**, **India**. It was established as a **Reserve Forest** in **1905**, declared a **National Park** in **1974**, and designated a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1985**.
 
• **The Big Five**: The park is globally recognized for conserving five major species: the **One-Horned Rhinoceros** (hosting over **2,600** individuals), the **Royal Bengal Tiger**, the **Asian Elephant**, the **Wild Water Buffalo**, and the **Eastern Swamp Deer** (Barasingha).

• **Flora and Avifauna**: The vegetation consists of **tall elephant grass**, marshland, and dense tropical moist broadleaf forests. It is also an **Important Bird Area (IBA)**, home to over **478 species** of birds, including migratory species from **Central Asia**.
